page: The Vultr vc2-4c-8gb is an entry-tier virtual machine belonging to the Cloud Compute product line. It is provisioned with 4 shared vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, running two threads per core. Memory allocation totals 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is locally bundled and consists of a 160 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by one included public IPv4 address. The configuration does not include a GPU accelerator.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate entry-level execution rates across CPU and memory subsystems, consistent with shared-host virtualization. In synthetic CPU profiling, the instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 936.0 and a multi-core score of 2888.0, alongside a PassMark CPU mark of 4794.79. Stress-ng measured 1265.69 for single-core and 4883.55 for multi-core performance, placing compute throughput in the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth remains restricted under large uncached transfers at 24.41 GB/s read and 19.55 GB/s write, although cached small-block reads registered 367.64 GB/s.

Application and operational metrics reflect modest throughput appropriate for light workloads. The instance handled Redis SET operations at 2.63 million operations per second and delivered static web serving throughput of 3.09 GB/s. Software compilation using Clang reached a Geekbench metric of 4183.0. In small-scale inference evaluations utilizing a 135M parameter language model, processing speed reached 211.43 prompt tokens per second and 46.35 generation tokens per second.

The primary operational tradeoff centers on CPU oversubscription. Because vCPUs are shared rather than dedicated, heavy computational jobs risk performance variance depending on concurrent host demand. Cost efficiency is balanced by the integration of fast NVMe storage alongside four execution threads. The vc2-4c-8gb is best aligned with staging environments, build workers, low-traffic web applications, microservices, and modest utility databases.

It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU, coupled with a bundled 160 GB NVMe SSD and one public IPv4 address, but no discrete GPU. Performance benchmarks position this instance in the entry-level tiers, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 2888.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 4794.79. Sustained uncached memory bandwidth sits below 25 GB/s, while Redis throughput reaches 2.63 million SET operations per second and web delivery achieves 3.09 GB/s. Due to shared hypervisor resources, it offers cost-efficient baseline throughput for dev-test setups, background tasks, lightweight web servers, and small internal services.
